item.title: Deep layoffs hit ‘The Washington Post,’ sparking sharp criticism for owner Jeff Bezos
item.description: The Washington Post informed its team on Wednesday morning that it was starting a round of mass layoffs, according to multiple media reports and a memo seen by Fast Company. item.description: Jeffrey Epstein’s network of money and influence often intersected with scientific and academic communities. item.title: Trump’s border czar pulls 700 immigration officers out of Minnesota
item.description: The Trump administration is reducing the number of immigration officers in Minnesota but will continue its enforcement operation that has sparked weeks of tensions and deadly confrontations, border czar Tom Homan said Wednesday. About 700 federal officers—roughly a quarter of the total deployed to Minnesota—will be withdrawn immediately after state and local officials agreed over the past week to cooperate by turning over arrested immigrants, Homan said. item.description: For a show that lasts roughly 13 minutes, the Super Bowl halftime performance has fueled decades of conversation. item.title: Amazon wants Alexa+ to be the reason you keep Prime
item.description: Amazon is rolling out a new feature in hopes of retaining—or perhaps attracting—new Prime members. The tech giant announced Wednesday that Alexa+, its AI-powered assistant, is now available for free to all Prime members. Last March, Amazon began offering an “early access” preview for the new voice assistant that saw an “inspiring” response, with tens of millions of customers requesting access, according to a statement. item.title: Some renters should be wary of ‘rent now, pay later’ services. Here’s why
item.description: Rent can eat up an entire paycheck at the start of the month, so a growing number of renters are turning to a financial product that promises relief by letting them split the bill — for a price. So-called “rent now, pay later” services have emerged over the past few years as housing costs climb and paychecks grow less predictable, particularly for lower-income and gig-economy workers. item.title: Doritos, Lays, Cheetos, and more popular snacks are getting a major discount ahead of the Super Bowl
item.description: Just in time for the Super Bowl, PepsiCo is cutting the price of Doritos, Cheetos, Lay’s, Tostitos, and other snacks by up to 15%. The move comes after consumers complained the chips were too pricey. “Our customers . . . have been honest with us about how rising everyday costs are making their daily decisions harder. item.title: Inside the Minneapolis restaurant that has stopped charging for food until ICE leaves the city
item.description: February is always difficult in Minneapolis. It’s when the nerve-flaying cold of December and January starts to seem like a dress rehearsal. But this February has proven brutal for other reasons. As thousands of Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents storm the city with lethal force, many residents have larger troubles than the arctic weather. item.title: Pizza Hut will close 250 ‘underperforming’ locations in 2026 as list of struggling restaurants grows
item.description: Pizza Hut is closing hundreds of “underperforming” locations nationwide, according to parent company Yum Brands, which reported fourth-quarter 2025 earnings on Wednesday. The company said it will shutter about 3% of Pizza Hut’s U.S. locations, or some 250 locations in the first six months of 2026, as the fast-causal chain struggles amid competition from Domino’s Pizza and an overall decline in store sales and consumer demand. item.title: Google parent Alphabet predicts a sharp surge in 2026 capital spending on AI
item.description: Alphabet said on Wednesday it was targeting capital expenditure of $175 billion to $185 billion this year, in yet another aggressive ramp-up in spending from the Google parent as it deepens its investments to push ahead in the AI race. Analysts on average had expected Alphabet to spend about $115.26 billion this year, according to data compiled by LSEG. Shares of the company fell more than 6% in extended trading.
